tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

content.text:
**Yes, your changes make sense, and they're built on the branch `fix/keep-valuations-sync-on-open`.** It isn't merged, so the Moneo you have running still has the old behaviour.

The real bug was that a late sync could change your net worth. That can't happen now: a value that's out of date stays in the total and gets flagged.

**What changes**
- **Old values stay counted:** only values dated in the future are left out. On your data, Home would show about €3,175.34 instead of €2,003.46 until the sync lands.
- **Warning names the items:** the new note looks like "6 valuations are not from today and use their last known value: Alphabet A, … (7 Nov 2026)". It appears on Home and Wealth, and chat and voice get the same list.
- **Sync on open:** opening or returning to the app shows the last numbers straight away, syncs in the background, then updates the page. Scalable syncs at most every 15 minutes and banks at most every hour, including after a failure.
- **Daily Scalable sync:** it now runs whenever the values aren't from today in your timezone, and retries hourly if it fails.
- **Failures show on Home:** for example "Scalable could not sync, so its numbers may be old", or "needs reconnecting", with a link to Settings.
- **Regression test:** a new test checks that the total doesn't change when the day rolls over.

**Testing**
- **Unit tests and lint:** all 1,424 unit tests that ran pass (10 skipped), and lint and the build pass. The last commit only adds a browser test.
- **Browser tests:** I ran only the specs this touches, not the full suite, and 3 of 4 passed. The new sync-on-open spec is one of the passes. The failure is `wealth.gated.spec.ts:22`, which expects wording the Wealth page no longer shows, so it fails on `main` too (#168).
- **Screenshots:** I checked the Home note on desktop in light mode and on mobile in dark mode, using the QA user.
- **Not tested:** a real bank or Scalable sync landing and updating the page, because the QA user has no connections and I didn't want to touch your real data. The on-open route's sync logic is only tested with mocks, so check this first after merging.

**Things to know**
- **Bank limits:** opening the app sends the same "user is present" signal as "Sync now", so per the existing code it shouldn't use the 4-a-day background allowance. Some banks might still rate-limit it. That would show on Home and the old numbers would stay.
- **Old manual assets:** something you valued a year ago now counts in full, with the note showing until you update it. That's what you asked for, but the total can include a very old value.
- **Month change:** after merging, Home will show about +€211.89 this month, which is misleading because Scalable wasn't in October's figure. That's tracked in #167.

Do you want me to merge this into `main`, rebuild and restart your app? The restart would stop the instance you have running, so I'll wait for your OK. The first open afterwards will run your first real sync through the new code, and I'd check that it lands.

questions.question: Which messages on the Net worth card should become a bottom-right toast instead of staying on the card? There are four kinds: the 'not from today' note, sync failures, 'Not counted: N items' (something is really missing from the total), and 'From 1 of 2 accounts. Fix 1 balance'.

options.label: Note and sync (Recommended)
options.description: 'Not from today' and sync failures become toasts. 'Not counted' and 'Fix 1 balance' stay on the card, because they mean the total is actually incomplete, and those are rarely shown.

options.label: All four
options.description: The card is completely clean. If you miss the toast, nothing on screen says the total is incomplete.

questions.question: How often should a toast come back for the same problem? It disappears by itself after a few seconds.

options.label: Once a day (Recommended)
options.description: Shows once per day for each problem, and again straight away if a new problem appears. Calm but you won't miss it for long.

options.label: Every app open
options.description: Shows each time you open or return to Moneo. Harder to miss, but could get annoying while a problem lasts.

options.label: Once per problem
options.description: Shows once and never again until the problem changes. Quietest, but easy to miss completely.

questions.question: After the toast goes away, should anything stay visible to show a value is old or a sync failed?

options.label: Tiny marker on card (Recommended)
options.description: A small dot or 'as of 7 Nov' beside Net worth; tapping it shows the full list. The card still looks clean, and the total never looks fresher than it is.

options.label: Only on Wealth
options.description: Home shows nothing after the toast. The Wealth page and Settings still show the details.

options.label: Nothing anywhere
options.description: Only the toast. The list is gone from every page once it disappears, apart from the 'As of' date on each item.

content.thinking:
I'm laying out the notices component: it takes a list of notices, shows them as a toast in the bottom right that fades after about eight seconds, and remembers which ones were already seen in localStorage. Now I'm working out what the key should be for an outdated notice, and whether it should depend on the text, which changes daily, or on the names and as_of date, so that it counts as a new problem only when the date changes.

I'm weighing whether the outdated-notice key should track the date instead of the text, since that would re-show a toast every morning before the sync lands. I'm considering a short hold before showing outdated notices so a quick sync on open can resolve them first, and I'm leaning toward keying on the item and its as_of date rather than the wording.

I'm weighing a fixed delay before the outdated-notice toast against having it wait on the sync finishing, since the sync can land a few seconds after open and then refresh the notices. Waiting on the sync settling seems cleaner, but the refresh can lag behind it, so a simple delay of around 20 seconds might be the safer choice.

I'm settling on a plain fixed delay of about 15 seconds before the outdated-notice toast, since the sync can take a while and bank failures get their own notice after the refresh anyway. An event-based wait would be more precise but more fiddly, and the timer only needs resetting when a notice key actually changes.

I'm going to verify the seen-tracking helper with a storage check rather than waiting for the toast to disappear, and keep the Wealth page's outdated note while dropping it from Home. Sync problems will stay visible in Settings, which already shows the last error.

I'm settling the toast's details now: it should only appear on Home, since that's where the notices are computed, with a link to Settings for sync problems and to Wealth for outdated valuations, plus a dismiss button. Long lists of names get clamped to a few lines, and I need to check the mobile bottom nav and any chat overlay so the toast sits above them, with an appropriate ARIA role.

I'm checking how the toast is positioned against the mobile bottom nav and any chat overlay, and whether the app already has an animation class I can reuse. I'm also planning a try/catch around the localStorage reads and writes, and deciding whether to show the toast on Home only.

I'm checking whether a fixed-position toast would get clipped by a transformed parent in the home grid, so I'm looking at the layout to decide whether to render it at the top of the main area instead of inside a widget.

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Glob, Grep, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- claude-security:claude-security: The Claude Security orchestrator, for use only as the main agent of a session (claude --agent claude-security:claude-security), where it runs a scan end to end and can turn its findings into targeted patch files, each verified by a panel of agents. Never dispatch it as a subagent: it cannot scan from there. When a user asks for Claude Security in a conversation, use the claude-security:claude-security skill instead. (Tools: Read, Glob, Grep, Bash, Write, Edit, AskUserQuestion, Workflow, Workflow(claude-security:scan), TaskCreate, TaskGet, TaskList, TaskUpdate, TaskOutput, TaskStop, Agent(claude-security:scan-inventory, claude-security:scan-researcher, claude-security:scan-verifier, claude-security:scan-loader, claude-security:scan-redactor, claude-security:patch-generator, claude-security:patch-verifier, claude-security:explore))

- claude-security:explore: Read-only code explorer that the plugin's other agents dispatch to map a codebase — locate files, trace how a flow is wired, find every caller of a symbol, answer "where does X happen". (Tools: Read, Glob, Grep, Bash)

- claude-security:patch-generator: Implements the fix for one finding inside a scratch workspace clone, staged for review and delivery as a patch file; dispatched by the fix job, not for direct invocation. (Tools: Read, Glob, Grep, Bash, Edit, Write, Agent(claude-security:explore))

- claude-security:patch-verifier: The single verifier per fix round — reviews the workspace's staged diff against the finding, runs the tests, and states the three confidence claims a patch file must earn; dispatched by the fix job, not for direct invocation. (Tools: Read, Glob, Grep, Bash, Agent(claude-security:explore))

- claude-security:scan-inventory: Restricted read-only repository cartographer dispatched by the Claude Security scan workflow to partition the tree into components and account for every top-level directory; not for direct invocation or vulnerability research. (Tools: Read, Glob, Grep)
- claude-security:scan-loader: Restricted read-only loader dispatched by the Claude Security scan workflow to return one JSON file from the run directory; not for direct invocation. (Tools: Read)

- claude-security:scan-redactor: Restricted agent dispatched by the Claude Security scan jobs to replace the credential values in a finished scan's report files with [REDACTED]; not for direct invocation. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- claude-security:scan-researcher: Restricted read-only vulnerability researcher dispatched by the Claude Security scan workflow; not for direct invocation or general exploration. (Tools: Read, Glob, Grep, Bash, Agent(claude-security:explore))

- claude-security:scan-verifier: Restricted read-only verifier dispatched by the Claude Security scan workflow to vote on one candidate finding; not for direct invocation. (Tools: Read, Glob, Grep, Bash, Agent(claude-security:explore))

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- awesome-design-md: Design systems extracted from 84 real websites (Airbnb, Apple, Stripe-style sites, Claude, Cursor, Figma and more) as DESIGN.md files. Use when the user asks to build or restyle UI "like" a named brand or site, or to match a visual design language.
- brand: Brand voice, visual identity, messaging frameworks, asset management, brand consistency. Activate for branded content, tone of voice, marketing assets, brand compliance, style guides.
- code-review: Review the changes since a fixed point (commit, branch, tag, or merge-base) along two axes: Standards (does the code follow this repo's documented coding standards?) and Spec (does the code match what the originating issue/spec asked for?). Runs both reviews in parallel sub-agents and reports them side by side. Use when the user wants to review a branch, a PR, work-in-progress changes, or asks to "review since X".
- codebase-design: Shared vocabulary for designing deep modules. Use when the user wants to design or improve a module's interface, find deepening opportunities, decide where a seam goes, make code more testable or AI-navigable, or when another skill needs the deep-module vocabulary.
- diagnosing-bugs: Diagnosis loop for hard bugs and performance regressions. Use when the user says "diagnose"/"debug this", or reports something broken/throwing/failing/slow.
- full-send: Trigger this if the user says 'full send'.
- full-stop: Trigger this if the user says 'full stop', even as a closing "Full stop." that reads like emphasis.
- prototype: Build a throwaway prototype to answer a design question. Use when the user wants to sanity-check whether a state model or logic feels right, or explore what a UI should look like.
- slides: Create strategic HTML presentations with Chart.js, design tokens, responsive layouts, copywriting formulas, and contextual slide strategies.
- sol-loop: Use when the user says "sol loop".
- tdd: Test-driven development. Use when the user wants to build features or fix bugs test-first, mentions "red-green-refactor", or wants integration tests.
- moneo-setup: Install, set up, start, update or troubleshoot Moneo on the user's own computer. Use when someone says "set up Moneo", "install Moneo", "Moneo won't start", or asks how to add their AI key, bank or Scalable Capital, or use Moneo on their phone or tablet.

# AGENTS.md

Moneo is an open-source personal-finance app you run on your own computer. One owner imports statements or syncs a bank, tracks accounts and wealth, plans spending, and asks about their money in chat, artifacts and voice calls.

Stack: Next.js 16 + React 19 + TypeScript. The backend is Postgres plus the open-source Supabase Auth, PostgREST and Storage services in Docker (`docker-compose.yml`). Drizzle schema, Workflow (local world) for durable jobs, Vitest and Playwright, and the Vercel AI SDK, paid by the owner's ChatGPT plan or an API key.

These are defaults. The developer's instructions override them; if a rule conflicts with the task, say so and ask.

## Non-negotiables

- **Local-first.** Everything listens on `127.0.0.1`; optional phone access is Tailscale forwarding to it (`lib/phone-access.ts`). Data leaves the machine only for services the owner set up (AI provider, Enable Banking, Scalable). New features must work fully offline from the cloud except those calls.
- **One owner, no accounts.** The proxy signs the owner in automatically; there is no sign-up or sign-in screen. Private access from the owner's own Tailscale devices needs no login; anything public must add one first.
- **Financial truth comes from code and data, never from AI guesses.** Money is integer minor units (`bigint`) with an explicit currency. The AI explains and proposes; every write it suggests is a card the owner accepts.
- **History is kept.** Preserve source records, corrections, history and undo when changing financial data flows.
- **Open source.** No secrets, private statements or personal data in the repo (`npm run check:privacy` runs before tests and lint).

## How to work

1. **Think before coding.** State your assumptions. If a request has more than one reading, name them and ask instead of picking silently. If a simpler approach exists, say so.
2. **Simplicity first.** Write the least code that solves the problem: no speculative features, options or single-use abstractions. Prefer existing utilities and dependencies, and Zod for validating user and external input. Would a senior engineer call it overcomplicated? Then simplify.
3. **Surgical changes.** Touch only what the task needs and match the nearby style. Remove what your own change made unused; mention unrelated dead code instead of deleting it.
4. **Goal-driven.** Turn the task into checks you can run, then loop until they pass. A bug fix starts with a test that fails on the current code. Purely visual changes get a before/after screenshot instead.

## Safety

- Never run tests or experiments against the owner's workspace. Browser tests use the QA user (`scripts/e2e-auth.mjs`) or disposable users they create and remove.
- Never delete the Docker volumes (`docker compose down -v`) or drop the database: that is the owner's financial history.
- Never change `JWT_SECRET`, `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` or `BANK_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY` in an existing `.env`; keys, sessions and stored bank and ChatGPT tokens stop working.
- Never commit `.env*` (except `.env.example`), `.data/`, `e2e/.auth.json` or `.qa/`.
- Only kill processes you started, or ones you verified by port and working directory. Never kill by name.
- Real AI, bank and Scalable calls cost money or count against limits (PSD2 allows about 4 background bank fetches a day). Mock them in tests unless the task is to check the real service.

## Hit every surface

Before calling a feature done, check where else it shows up:

- Pages and their mobile layout, light and dark.
- Chat tools and the system prompt in `lib/ai/provider.ts`, artifacts, and the voice call (`lib/ai/voice-*`).
- Home widgets and the command palette.
- Background jobs (`lib/scheduler.ts`, `workflows/`) and imports from files, banks and Scalable.
- The reverse path: undo, reset all data, reconnect, disconnect.
- Docs: `README.md` for anything the owner sets up or runs, `.env.example` for new variables. Deferred work goes in GitHub issues.

## Commands

Use npm (`package-lock.json` is authoritative).

- Install: `npm ci`
- Backend: `npm run setup` (writes `.env` secrets, starts Docker, applies migrations, creates the owner; safe to rerun)
- Dev: `npm run dev` (http://localhost:3000)
- Unit: `npm test` · Lint: `npm run lint` · Build: `npm run build`
- E2E: `npm run test:e2e` (see `e2e/README.md`)

## Project map

- `app/` — App Router pages, route handlers, server actions
- `lib/finance/` — deterministic financial logic
- `lib/ai/` — models, chat tools, ChatGPT sign-in (`chatgpt.ts`), voice
- `lib/bank/`, `lib/scalable/` — Enable Banking and Scalable Capital
- `lib/schema.ts` + `supabase/migrations/` — database schema
- `workflows/` — durable background jobs; `lib/scheduler.ts` runs the daily ones
- `docker-compose.yml`, `docker/`, `scripts/setup.mjs` — the self-hosted backend
- `e2e/` — Playwright flows; `supabase/tests/` — SQL regressions

## Sign-in callbacks and addresses

Each outside service sends the browser back to a different address. Keep these in mind before changing ports, hosts or remote access:

- **Sign in with ChatGPT** (`lib/ai/chatgpt.ts`): OpenAI only accepts the loopback `http://127.0.0.1:<PORT>/api/ai/chatgpt/callback`, so sign-in happens on the computer running Moneo. Tokens are stored there, so chat works from any device afterwards.
- **Enable Banking** (`lib/bank/return-listener.ts`): production apps need an `https://` redirect registered in the Enable Banking app. Moneo uses `https://localhost:3443/api/bank/callback` (a local listener with a cert from `npm run setup`), which forwards to `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL`.
- **Scalable Capital** (`lib/scalable/server.ts`): dynamic client registration with `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL/api/scalable/callback`. `localhost` registers freely; other hosts need Scalable's allowlist (it rejects `*.ts.net`).
- **Supabase** (`NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`, `127.0.0.1:54321`): only the server may call it; never send the browser there, or it breaks on other devices.
- **Phone and tablet** (`*.ts.net` through Tailscale Serve): the laptop's addresses above never change. The three logins refuse to start from a remote device (`lib/remote-device.ts`) and say to use the computer; everything else, including sync, works from there.
- **Voice** needs a secure context (https or localhost) for the microphone.

## Database changes

Add a new ordered migration in `supabase/migrations/` and keep `lib/schema.ts` aligned. Never rewrite an applied migration. `npm run setup` applies pending ones and records them in `supabase_migrations.schema_migrations`. For other Supabase CLI commands use `npx supabase ... --db-url "$SUPABASE_DB_URL"` (from `.env`).

## Validation

Run the smallest relevant test while iterating. Before finishing, run `npm test` and `npm run lint`; add `npm run build` for app, config or build changes, and Playwright for changed user flows. Await real events in tests; don't add sleeps or polling.

## Commits and pull requests

- Break the work into steps and commit each one; a big task is several commits.
- Never open a pull request unless asked.
- Write commit messages in plain language: what changed and why.
- Deferred work gets their issue created on github.
- suggest edits in agents.md if there was something that is changed or needs to be there in agents.md but only suggest when it is actually needed dont suggest just for suggesting.(only for prs)

## Context

Read only what the task needs: `.env.example` for environment names, `e2e/README.md` for browser tests, `supabase/tests/README.md` for SQL checks.

# This is NOT the Next.js you know

This version has breaking changes — APIs, conventions, and file structure may all differ from your training data. Read the relevant guide in `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` (resolved from this file's directory; in monorepos the `next` package may not be visible from the repo root) before writing any code. Heed deprecation notices.

This block is written and re-added by `next dev` — verify at `node_modules/next/dist/server/lib/generate-agent-files.js`. Removing it from a diff only re-creates the uncommitted change; committing it with your work keeps the tree clean.

- [lib workflow tests need OPENAI key](lib-workflow-tests-need-openai-key.md) — 14 lib/ tests fail on main without OPENAI_API_KEY
- [Python edits need UTF-8](python-edits-need-utf8.md) — open() is cp1252 here; non-ASCII gets corrupted
- [AI keys for dev](qa-chat-needs-openrouter-model.md) — OpenRouter out of credits 2026-10-27; OpenAI key (gpt-live-1) in main and voice worktree .env since 2026-10-30
- [Cash balance default account](cash-balance-default-account.md) — stated cash goes to the currency's cash account; create or ask when none or several
- [Voice feature branch workflow](voice-feature-branch-workflow.md) — PRs go into t3/voice-finance-agent; user opens final PR to main; ignore Entire gate
- [Voice design decisions](voice-design-decisions.md) — GPT-Live hands off to /api/chat, parallel tasks without a limit, tap-only cards, one mic with Send/Done
- [Overnight autonomy and subagent models](overnight-autonomy-and-subagent-models.md) — decide with my recommendation and report later; subagents use Opus 5.5 low or Sonnet 5.5; test voice against the real API
- [Audit fix decisions](audit-fix-decisions.md) — forecast with coverage, proposal default account rules, privacy contact address
- [Perf measurement setup](perf-measurement-setup.md) — measure on a prod build with a seeded QA workspace; React cache() is a no-op in route handlers
- [UI feedback pass decisions](ui-feedback-pass-decisions.md) — no cash-flow in net worth, masonry home grid, Ask-only ledger search, hidden scrollbars
- [Self-hosted pivot](self-hosted-pivot.md) — open-source self-hosted via Docker; keep local Supabase pieces; ChatGPT sign-in and API key equal; phone access via private Tailscale
- [Scalable trading decisions](scalable-trading-decisions.md) — card-only buy/sell/cancel, no limit, previews only on real account
- [Artifact Scalable + sliders](artifact-scalable-and-slider-decisions.md) — snapshot default with Settings live toggle; Pages keep JS; card sliders rerun in browser QuickJS
