tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

content.text:
**Moneo doesn't do the full calculation.** Today's value is correct, but your history only starts from the day you connected Scalable, which was 7 November.

**How it works now**

| What you see | Where it comes from | Goes back to |
|---|---|---|
| Value today | Scalable's current holdings: quantity × live price, plus cash and crypto | Now only |
| Gain per stock | Scalable's own average buy price (FIFO) | All time, but as one figure |
| Return for a period, like one month | Scalable's own figure | Those periods only, with no day-by-day history |
| Scalable value chart and "this month" | A saved copy of the values from each sync | 7 November |
| Bank balances | Balances from each sync, plus imported transactions | Only as far as Moneo has them (earliest saved balance is 30 October) |

So Moneo doesn't replay what you bought or when. Before 7 November it treats your Scalable value as nothing, which is why a newly connected portfolio looks like a gain (#167).

**What the full calculation would take**

Moneo already calls Scalable for what this needs, but only in small pieces. For each day it would:
1. Replay all your buys, sells, deposits, withdrawals and dividends to get what you held and your cash.
2. Multiply each holding by that day's price, using Scalable's price chart.
3. Save those as past-dated values, marked as calculated. The charts and "this month" should then use them with little change.

**How easy:** moderate, about one focused feature, and no change to the main net worth rule. The hard parts are:
- **Unknowns in Scalable's data:** I haven't seen how far its transaction list goes back, or whether the "max" price chart has daily prices for older dates. A read-only check on your account would answer this first.
- **Crypto:** Moneo reads coin history differently, and the price chart is looked up by ISIN (the stock ID), which coins may not have. Crypto may have to stay from 7 November onwards.
- **Stock splits and similar events:** these change share counts without a normal buy or sell, so the replay has to handle them.

**How I'd build it**
- **Accuracy check:** the replay must end at exactly the holdings and cash Scalable reports today. If it doesn't, Moneo saves nothing and keeps the history starting from 7 November, so it never shows a wrong past.
- **Labelling:** calculated days are marked as calculated, so they stay separate from real synced values.
- **Your bank accounts:** this wouldn't extend their history. That depends on how far back your bank shares data, though you can fill older periods by importing statements.

This would fix #167 for Scalable, but not for a newly connected bank.

Do you want me to run the read-only check first? It tells us how far back this can go before anything gets built. The merged work on your local `main` isn't affected, so you can still tell me to push it separately.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.sync_scalable_wealth(p_connection_id uuid, p_items jsonb, p_portfolio jsonb)                                                                                     +
  RETURNS integer                                                                                                                                                                                   +
  LANGUAGE plpgsql                                                                                                                                                                                  +
  SECURITY DEFINER                                                                                                                                                                                  +
  SET search_path TO ''                                                                                                                                                                             +
 AS $function$                                                                                                                                                                                      +
 declare connection public.scalable_connections%rowtype; owner uuid; entry jsonb; previous public.wealth_items%rowtype; item public.wealth_items%rowtype;                                           +
   existing boolean; kept uuid[] := '{}'; changed integer := 0;                                                                                                                                     +
 begin                                                                                                                                                                                              +
   if p_connection_id is null or jsonb_typeof(p_items) is distinct from 'array' or jsonb_typeof(p_portfolio) is distinct from 'object' then                                                         +
     raise exception 'Invalid Scalable sync' using errcode = '22023'; end if;                                                                                                                       +
   select * into connection from public.scalable_connections where id = p_connection_id and status = 'active' for update;                                                                           +
   if not found then raise exception 'Scalable connection is not active' using errcode = 'P0002'; end if;                                                                                           +
   select owner_id into owner from public.workspaces where id = connection.workspace_id;                                                                                                            +
   for entry in select value from jsonb_array_elements(p_items) loop                                                                                                                                +
     if entry - array['id','kind','name','currency_code','amount_minor','quantity_text','unit_price_text','cost_basis_minor','as_of'] <> '{}'::jsonb                                                +
       or entry->>'kind' not in ('holding','asset') then raise exception 'Unsupported Scalable wealth fields' using errcode = '22023'; end if;                                                      +
     item := jsonb_populate_record(null::public.wealth_items, entry);                                                                                                                               +
     if item.as_of > (now() at time zone coalesce((select timezone from public.workspace_settings where workspace_id = connection.workspace_id), 'Europe/Berlin'))::date then                       +
       raise exception 'Valuation date cannot be in the future' using errcode = '22023'; end if;                                                                                                    +
     select * into previous from public.wealth_items where id = item.id for update;                                                                                                                 +
     existing := found;                                                                                                                                                                             +
     if existing and previous.workspace_id <> connection.workspace_id then raise exception 'Wealth item belongs to another workspace' using errcode = '42501'; end if;                              +
     if existing and (previous.kind <> item.kind or previous.currency_code <> item.currency_code) then raise exception 'Scalable position changed kind or currency' using errcode = '22023'; end if;+
     kept := kept || item.id;                                                                                                                                                                       +
     if existing and previous.removed_at is null and previous.name = item.name and previous.amount_minor = item.amount_minor and previous.as_of = item.as_of                                        +
       and previous.quantity_text is not distinct from item.quantity_text and previous.unit_price_text is not distinct from item.unit_price_text                                                    +
       and previous.cost_basis_minor is not distinct from item.cost_basis_minor then continue; end if;                                                                                              +
     item.workspace_id := connection.workspace_id; item.version := coalesce(previous.version, 0) + 1; item.created_at := coalesce(previous.created_at, now());                                      +
     item.updated_at := now(); item.removed_at := null;                                                                                                                                             +
     insert into public.wealth_items select item.* on conflict (id) do update set name = excluded.name, amount_minor = excluded.amount_minor,                                                       +
       quantity_text = excluded.quantity_text, unit_price_text = excluded.unit_price_text, cost_basis_minor = excluded.cost_basis_minor, as_of = excluded.as_of,                                    +
       version = excluded.version, removed_at = null, updated_at = excluded.updated_at;                                                                                                             +
     insert into public.wealth_events(workspace_id, item_id, actor_id, request_id, before, after)                                                                                                   +
       values (connection.workspace_id, item.id, owner, gen_random_uuid(), case when existing then public.wealth_record(previous) end, public.wealth_record(item));                                 +
     changed := changed + 1;                                                                                                                                                                        +
   end loop;                                                                                                                                                                                        +
   -- Positions an earlier sync (from any connection of this workspace) wrote that Scalable no longer reports were sold.                                                                            +
   for previous in select w.* from public.wealth_items w where w.workspace_id = connection.workspace_id and w.removed_at is null and not (w.id = any(kept))                                         +
     and w.id in (select (jsonb_array_elements_text(c.portfolio->'itemIds'))::uuid from public.scalable_connections c where c.workspace_id = connection.workspace_id and c.portfolio ? 'itemIds')   +
     for update loop                                                                                                                                                                                +
     item := previous; item.removed_at := now(); item.version := previous.version + 1; item.updated_at := now();                                                                                    +
     update public.wealth_items set removed_at = item.removed_at, version = item.version, updated_at = item.updated_at where id = item.id;                                                          +
     insert into public.wealth_events(workspace_id, item_id, actor_id, request_id, before, after)                                                                                                   +
       values (connection.workspace_id, item.id, owner, gen_random_uuid(), public.wealth_record(previous), public.wealth_record(item));                                                             +
     changed := changed + 1;                                                                                                                                                                        +
   end loop;                                                                                                                                                                                        +
   update public.scalable_connections set portfolio = p_portfolio || jsonb_build_object('itemIds', to_jsonb(kept)), last_synced_at = now(), last_error = null                                       +
     where id = p_connection_id;                                                                                                                                                                    +
   return changed;                                                                                                                                                                                  +
 end;                                                                                                                                                                                               +
 $function$                                                                                                                                                                                         +
